analysis.title: 'Cash Is King, But Where Is He Hiding?': Goldman's Basket Desk Builds An AI Barbell As Momentum Breaks Down
key_insights: Goldman's custom baskets desk says the post-election relief rally lasted under 24 hours and AI/geopolitics fatigue resumed. It recommends a barbell of selective AI trades plus defensive, immediate FCF/income generators.

Last week's tech momentum crash and hedge fund degross set up an AI rebound, but the market's appetite to digest NVDA-specific issues was short lived. The desk says whether this is a buy-the-dip or a regime shift in equity leadership depends on whether the market is in an earnings bubble.

Goldman says certain pockets of the market are clearly over earning, but some valuations have overshot to the downside. Korean memory is the example, with prices calling for excessive downward revisions to 2027 earnings.

At a KOSPI semi sector price-to-book of 2.6x, Goldman's Korea team calculates the market is pricing a 65% cut to forward 12-month earnings. If earnings hold, the implied upside is 176% (priced as of Oct 22). Current earnings carry a 60% operating margin, 4.2 standard deviations above the historical norm.

Pockets of defensive AI exposure the desk still likes: the Power theme (GSENEPOW) is up since the midterms, IPPs (GSXUIPPS) are +15% off their lows, and the Hyperscalers basket (GSXUHYPR) is where the desk would hide inside the AI theme.
To balance AI exposure, Goldman likes adding longs in the S&P ex-AI index (SPXXAI), which has outperformed the SPX over the past year (+16.7% vs +12.0%) and held up better in last week's selloff.

Hyperscaler capex is eating free cash flow, which went negative in Q3 per the article. Goldman says the market's biggest index weights now lack FCF, non-cash earnings are a bigger share of earnings growth, and it expects the market to keep rewarding high FCF generators.

The desk's preferred FCF expression is its US High vs Low Free Cash Flow pair (GSPUFCFP). Since July, High FCF names are up about 6% and Low FCF names are down about 9%, with the outperformance equally driven by the long and short legs, unlike Quality where gains came mostly from shorts falling.

The European FCF pair (GSPEFCFP) lagged over the summer but has started to aggressively catch up, and Goldman expects that to continue. The matching short is the Lending Sensitive basket (GSXULEND), companies that may get crowded out by other capital market needs.

China High Dividend basket (GSXACHHN), heavy in banks and energy/utilities, has delivered +8pp over three months while the CSI 300 declined 15pp. Goldman cites stable cash generation, attractive yields, domestic earnings and National Team buying.

Europe has one of the lowest betas to the AI trade (SXXP 2y daily beta to GSPUARTI below 0.05). Goldman expects investors to return to the region for AI diversification, and European equity funds took in $35.1 billion in the week to Wednesday, the most since June 2021.

Goldman says the real European bull case hinges on a US-Iran resolution. In the interim the desk likes its EU High and Stable Margins basket (GSXEMARG), about 4 points ahead of the Euro Stoxx 50 over the past year and recently breaking out.

Goldman thinks the rally in French Domestics (GSXEFRDO), up 10% from October lows, is premature. The OAT-Bund spread has barely recovered at around 154bps, credit conditions remain difficult and political uncertainty is high. The near-term catalyst is S&P's credit rating review on November 27.

Goldman flags a momentum regime shift. The correlation between 12m momentum (GSPRHIMO) and 3m momentum (GSPRHMO3) is now negative, the number of AI names in the short leg of 3m and 6m momentum has skyrocketed, and infotech was net sold in 3m and 6m momentum but slightly bought in 12m.

60-day realized vol on Goldman's high beta momentum basket is about 54, roughly 3.5x the S&P's 15, down from a peak near 85 in October. Goldman expects rotations and reversals to stay a feature of the factor until the market settles on new long-term leadership.

ZeroHedge commentary (not Goldman): the author would lean harder on the defensive end of the barbell, arguing that a market over earning in its most crowded corner is more likely to see margins mean-revert than double. Cited context is Nvidia's first quarter without its CEO reporting Tuesday, followed by the Anthropic IPO a day later.

tension_points.bull_case: At a price-to-book of 2.6x the market prices a 65% earnings cut, so any reignition of AI confidence could drive a doubling of memory stocks (176% implied upside if earnings hold).
tension_points.bear_case: Current earnings carry a 60% operating margin, 4.2 standard deviations above norm, and the article says Washington's tolerance for soaring memory costs is ending, so the margins may be cyclical rather than permanent.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Whether the fat margins prove cyclical or permanent, tied to whether the market is in an earnings bubble.

tension_points.bull_case: The basket is up 10% from October lows as French politics took a backseat.
tension_points.bear_case: The OAT-Bund spread has barely recovered at around 154bps, credit conditions remain difficult and political uncertainty is high, leaving scope for the downtrend to resume.
tension_points.what_invalidates: S&P's credit rating review of France on November 27, where a downgrade would favor the bear case.
